source.title: Hand to Hand Kettle Bell Swing

sourceFacts: Review the two-hand swing before alternating hand changes.
The lesson demonstrates thumb-back to thumb-up at the change and emphasizes controlled parking.
One-handed support introduces cross-body stabilization; numerical superiority or a universal optimal program is not inferred.
appDecisions: Explicit familiar hand-change confirmation and recent qualified two-hand swing practice.
Count each swing for its driving hand, prescribe 3–5 per hand, start with 2–4 sets and 90-second rests; all numerical doses and count conventions are app defaults.
Dedicated opt-in block, independent cycle and deliberate owned single-bell load review. No automatic new gate is added to existing paired histories.
limits: No numerical hand-to-hand program or breathing cadence is provided by #185.
Release/catch timing requires reviewing the demonstrated video; no timestamps are verified.
Broader one-arm swings, outside swings and full paired preparation remain incomplete.

entry.purpose: Practice alternating hand changes while the trunk controls rotation during a familiar single-kettlebell swing.
setup: Establish a comfortable controlled two-hand swing first, using a familiar manageable bell and clear space.
Review the demonstrated hand change before confirming the separate skill. The app does not prescribe overhead hand changes.
steps: Begin with the reviewed two-hand swing pattern: hinge back with grounded heels and supported shoulders.
For the hand-change version, begin with the thumb pointing back, stand and turn the thumb up for the demonstrated change to the other hand.
Continue alternating hands with a controlled trunk. In the app, count each swing for the hand that drives it and match the counts on both sides.
Finish and park the bell with the same controlled technique used at the start.
bracing: Maintain trunk control as one hand takes the load; the source discusses cross-body stabilization and resisting rotation.
This transcript does not specify a compulsory breathing cadence. Retain familiar controlled breathing rather than inventing a new timed breath sequence.
mistakes: Uncontrolled release or reaching awkwardly to force a change: stop, review the video and return to the familiar two-hand swing.
Hurrying the set-down or dropping the bell on the last rep: finish with the same control as the first rep.
Counting five swings total as five per hand: the app prescribes and records actual driving-hand counts separately; five per hand means ten alternating swings.
Repetitions do not certify release/catch technique. Text and app confirmations do not replace reviewing the demonstrated hand path.
